takeaways: Record revenue of $267.8 million, up 73%, beat the $257.2 million estimate and topped the company's own $258-265 million guide.
The loss was wider than expected: −$0.12 a share vs −$0.07 expected (Investing.com), partly on a $27.3 million debt-extinguishment loss and $21.3 million of deal costs.
Backlog jumped $1.2 billion in one quarter to $3.57 billion, with about $1 billion of new launch contracts; Neutron now has 16 missions booked, first launch no earlier than 2027.
Q4 guide: revenue $270-290 million, non-GAAP gross margin 39-41%, adjusted EBITDA loss of $14-20 million.
The stock ran up 10.9% on Monday into the print, then slipped after hours (Investing.com).
verdict: Rocket Lab sold more space than ever and the backlog grew like it ate a whole constellation. But the stock rallied 11% into the report, the loss came in wider and Neutron is still a 2027 story. Great quarter, priced for a perfect one.
